particle.usage: n.微粒；极少量；粒子；part(部分)+icle(小)→很小的部分→微粒

ex.en: These very particles can penetrate deep into the lungs.
ex.zh: 这些小的尘埃可深深地吸入肺部。

ex.en: Dust particles in the air can carry bacteria and viruses over surprisingly long distances.
ex.zh: 空气中的尘埃颗粒能携带细菌和病毒传播到惊人的距离。

ex.en: Physicists smash particles together at high speed to study the basic building blocks of matter.
ex.zh: 物理学家让粒子高速对撞，以研究物质的基本构成。

senses: adj. ①特殊的，特别的 ②特定的，特指的
③细致的 ④苛求的，挑剔的
adj. 专指的，特别的，独特的
adj. 特指的；特殊的；尤其的；挑剔的

ex.en: These documents are of particular interest.
ex.zh: 这些文件让人尤其感兴趣。

ex.en: She is very particular about the cleanliness of her kitchen.
ex.zh: 她对厨房的清洁非常讲究。

ex.en: The report focuses on one particular region where unemployment has risen fastest.
ex.zh: 该报告聚焦于失业率上升最快的一个特定地区。

ex.en: The essay traces how religious particularism gradually gave way to a shared national identity during the country's industrialization.
ex.zh: 文章追溯了在该国工业化进程中，宗教特殊主义如何逐渐让位于共同的民族认同。

ex.en: Critics argue that a particularist approach to history ignores the shared features of different cultures.
ex.zh: 批评者认为，排他主义的历史研究方法忽视了不同文化之间的共同特征。

particularly.usage: adv.非常，尤其；特别是；易混词辨析:specially表示专门目的,强调“专门地”;especially指超乎一般的重要,达到显眼或例外的程度,强调独特性;particularly指与同类事物不同的个别事物；索引p413

ex.en: The visitors were particularly impressed with the dessert.
ex.zh: 游客们对甜点印象特别深刻。

ex.en: The tax change affects small firms particularly badly.
ex.zh: 税收调整对小企业的冲击尤为严重。

ex.en: It is particularly important to check the contract before signing it.
ex.zh: 签字之前核对合同尤为重要。

senses: adj. (盲目)支持的,偏袒的;有倾向性的
n. 游击队员;信徒,党羽

ex.en: The committee's report was dismissed as partisan criticism, because every recommendation favoured one political party over the others.
ex.zh: 该委员会的报告被斥为带有党派偏见的批评，因为每项建议都偏向某一个政党。

ex.en: The delay was partly caused by the extreme weather last winter.
ex.zh: 延误的部分原因是去年冬天的极端天气。

ex.en: The road was partly blocked by a fallen tree.
ex.zh: 道路被一棵倒下的树部分堵住。

ex.en: He succeeded partly because of talent, but mostly through sheer hard work.
ex.zh: 他的成功部分源于天赋，但主要靠纯粹的勤奋。

partner.usage: 派生 partnership n. 合作；合资企业

ex.en: My partner is kind as well as hospitable.
ex.zh: 我的搭档既善良又热情。

ex.en: After five years with the firm she was made a partner.
ex.zh: 在这家公司工作五年后，她成了合伙人。

ex.en: Dancers must learn to trust their partners completely.
ex.zh: 舞者必须学会完全信任自己的舞伴。

senses: n. 合伙关系；合作关系
n. 合伙人身份；伙伴关系

ex.en: Marriage should be an equal partnership.
ex.zh: 婚姻应当是平等的伴侣关系。

senses: n. 聚会;政党,党派;一方;当事人

ex.en: Each party to the contract is legally bound to fulfill the obligations listed in the agreement.
ex.zh: 合同的每一方在法律上都有义务履行协议中列明的责任。

senses: vt.&vi. 通过；走过；及格；合格
vi. 推移；结束；n. 及格；通行证

ex.en: Only candidates who pass the final interview will be considered for the position.
ex.zh: 只有通过最终面试的候选人才能被考虑录用。

ex.en: According to the passage, rising sea levels pose a serious threat to low-lying island nations.
ex.zh: 根据这篇短文，海平面上升对地势低洼的岛国构成严重威胁。

senses: n. 乘客，旅客；不做分内事的成员

ex.en: Every passenger must fasten the seat belt before the plane takes off.
ex.zh: 每位乘客在飞机起飞前都必须系好安全带。

ex.en: A passer-by called the emergency services immediately after noticing smoke rising from the old building.
ex.zh: 一名路人注意到旧楼冒出浓烟后立即拨打了急救电话。

ex.en: A passerby stopped to help the elderly woman who had slipped on the icy pavement.
ex.zh: 一位过路人停下来帮助在结冰的人行道上滑倒的老妇人。

phrases.p: throw himself into a hobby or a passion project
phrases.m: （他自己）投入一种爱好或者一项激情四溢的活动

passion.usage: n.激情，热情；热衷的爱好；发音类似"拍心(胸膛)"→说话总拍着胸脯的人多有激情啊；串词记忆：年轻人对时尚(fashion)充满激情(passion)；索引p413

ex.en: She has a great passion for classical music.
ex.zh: 她对古典音乐有着极大的热情。

ex.en: His passion for environmental protection led him to study ecology.
ex.zh: 他对环保的热情促使他去学习生态学。

ex.en: A successful career often begins with a genuine passion for the work.
ex.zh: 成功的事业往往始于对工作真挚的热情。

senses: adj. 情意绵绵的；怒不可遏的

ex.en: If that happens, passionate consumers would try to persuade others to boycott products.
ex.zh: 如果那种事情发生，激动的消费者将会试图劝服其他人抵制产品。

ex.en: He is passionate about protecting the environment and gives talks in local schools.
ex.zh: 他热心于环境保护，并到当地学校演讲。

ex.en: The young lawyer made a passionate speech in defense of the workers.
ex.zh: 这位年轻律师发表了慷慨激昂的演讲，为工人们辩护。

ex.en: She spoke passionately about the need to protect endangered species, drawing on her fifteen years of fieldwork in the rainforest.
ex.zh: 她满怀热情地讲述了保护濒危物种的必要性，并援引了她在雨林中十五年野外考察的经历。

passive.usage: adj.消极的，被动的；被动语 态的 n.被动语态；pass（过）+ive（形容词后缀）→很难从过去走出来，非常消极→消极的

ex.en: We are passive recipients of information from the world around us.
ex.zh: 我们被动地接收周围世界的信息。

ex.en: Teachers complain that online lectures encourage passive learning among students.
ex.zh: 教师们抱怨网络讲座助长了学生的被动学习。

ex.en: He played a passive role in the negotiations, letting his deputy speak for the group.
ex.zh: 他在谈判中扮演被动角色，让副手代表小组发言。

senses: n. 护照；(达到某种目的的)手段(c)

ex.en: Travelers are advised to check that their passport remains valid for at least six months before departure.
ex.zh: 建议旅行者在出发前确认护照有效期至少还有六个月。

ex.en: Security experts advise users to change their passwords regularly and never to reuse the same one across multiple accounts.
ex.zh: 安全专家建议用户定期更换密码，切勿在多个账户中重复使用同一密码。

ex.en: In the past, workers spent decades with a single company; today job changes are far more common.
ex.zh: 过去，工人往往在一家公司工作几十年；如今更换工作要常见得多。

ex.en: You can copy and paste the data into a spreadsheet for further statistical analysis.
ex.zh: 你可以把这些数据复制并粘贴到电子表格中，作进一步的统计分析。

senses: n. 彩色粉笔,粉蜡笔;彩色粉笔画,蜡笔画

ex.en: The artist abandoned bright oils for soft pastels, believing their gentle tones better suited the quiet landscapes she wanted to paint.
ex.zh: 这位艺术家放弃了色彩鲜艳的油画颜料，改用柔和的粉蜡笔，因为她相信粉蜡笔淡雅的色调更适合她想画的宁静风景。

pastime.usage: pas（通过）+time（时间）→让时间流逝的方式→消遣。近recreation n.娱乐；hobby n.爱好

ex.en: Gardening has become a popular pastime among urban residents seeking relief from work pressure.
ex.zh: 园艺已成为希望缓解工作压力的城市居民中流行的一种消遣。

ex.en: Nutritionists point out that many popular pastries contain high levels of sugar and saturated fat, despite their appealing appearance.
ex.zh: 营养学家指出，尽管外观诱人，许多受欢迎的糕点都含有大量的糖和饱和脂肪。

ex.en: The sheep were left to graze on the open pasture throughout the summer months.
ex.zh: 整个夏季，羊群都被放养在开阔的牧场上吃草。

senses: adj. 不自然的；油滑的；过于简单的

ex.en: The coach gave the young player a pat on the back to encourage her after the defeat.
ex.zh: 比赛失利后，教练轻拍年轻球员的后背以示鼓励。

senses: n. 补丁,补片;小块土地

phrases.m: 修补;拼凑成;暂时解决(分歧、争吵等)

ex.en: Farmers were forced to abandon the last green patch of farmland as the desert kept spreading.
ex.zh: 由于沙漠不断扩张，农民被迫放弃了最后一块绿色的农田。

senses: n. 拼布工艺(品);拼缝物,拼凑的东西,杂烩
patchwork.usage: 组合词：patch(小块)+work(工作)→一小块一小块的工作模块→拼凑的；索引p413

ex.en: The countryside from the air resembles a patchwork of fields, forests, and small villages.
ex.zh: 从空中俯瞰，乡村宛如由农田、森林和小村庄拼成的一幅拼布。

senses: n. 专利,专利权,专利品
adj. 专利的,特许的;受专利保护的
vt. 批准专利,获得专利
patent.usage: [族] patentee n. 专利获得者；pa(发音似pay付款)+tent(帐篷)→付款才能拥有有"专利"的帐篷；另：a patent attorney专利律师；anti-patent trend反专利风潮；a claimed patent已申请过的专利；索引p413

ex.en: The device was protected by patent.
ex.zh: 这一装置受专利保护。

ex.en: The company patented its new battery design before publishing any details of the research.
ex.zh: 该公司在公布研究细节之前就为新电池设计申请了专利。

ex.en: Filing a patent can cost thousands of dollars, which deters many small inventors.
ex.zh: 申请专利可能花费数千美元，这使许多小发明家望而却步。

ex.en: Lawyers disagree over whether software algorithms should be regarded as patentable inventions under the current legal framework.
ex.zh: 律师们对软件算法在现行法律框架下是否应被视为可授予专利的发明存在分歧。

ex.en: He showed a paternal concern for the welfare of his young employees.
ex.zh: 他对年轻员工的福祉表现出父亲般的关怀。

ex.en: Her paternal grandfather was a farmer who never left the village.
ex.zh: 她的祖父是农民，一生从未离开过村庄。

ex.en: The company was criticized for its paternal attitude toward its workers.
ex.zh: 这家公司因对员工采取家长式态度而受到批评。

ex.en: The court ordered a paternity test to determine who should take financial responsibility for the child.
ex.zh: 法院下令进行亲子鉴定，以确定谁应承担抚养孩子的经济责任。

path.usage: 近route, way；n.小径，小道；路线，途径

ex.en: A narrow path leads from the village to the top of the hill.
ex.zh: 一条小径从村庄通向山顶。

ex.en: After years in business, she chose an academic path instead.
ex.zh: 经商多年后，她转而选择了学术道路。

ex.en: The new law opens a path to citizenship for long-term residents.
ex.zh: 新法律为长期居民开辟了一条入籍之路。

senses: adj. 可怜的，可悲的，令人怜惜的；无力的
pathetic.usage: path（感情）+-etic→令人动情的→可怜的。勿与sympathetic（同情的）混淆；派生pathetically adv.可怜地

ex.en: She made a pathetic attempt to smile.
ex.zh: 她勉强地微微一笑。

ex.en: The team's performance in the second half was absolutely pathetic.
ex.zh: 球队下半场的表现糟糕透顶。

ex.en: The abandoned dog gave a pathetic whine when the door closed.
ex.zh: 门关上时，被遗弃的狗发出可怜的哀叫。

senses: n. 小路,小径;道路;途径

ex.en: The government has promised to create a clear pathway to citizenship for long-term migrant workers and their families.
ex.zh: 政府承诺为长期外来务工人员及其家庭创建一条明确的入籍途径。

ex.en: True empathy allows doctors to understand their patients' suffering without being overwhelmed by it.
ex.zh: 真正的同理心能让医生理解病人的痛苦，而又不被这种痛苦压垮。

patience.usage: [近] endurance n. 忍耐力；[反] impatience n. 不耐烦，无耐心；扩展:patient adj.有耐心的;patiently adv.耐心地；陪伴病人(patient)需要很大的耐心(patience)；索引p413

ex.en: I have run out of patience with her.
ex.zh: 我对她已失去耐心了。

ex.en: Teaching young children requires enormous patience and understanding.
ex.zh: 教幼儿需要极大的耐心和理解。

ex.en: After hours of waiting, the passengers finally lost their patience.
ex.zh: 等了几个小时后，乘客们终于失去了耐心。

patient.usage: adj.有耐心的 n.病人，患者；patience 的派生词；串词记忆:对专利证书(patent)的取得要有耐心(patient)；索引p413

ex.en: Children of every age benefit from patient parenting.
ex.zh: 每个年龄的孩子都受益于耐心的养育。

ex.en: It is not enough to say that the algorithms DeepMind develops will benefit patients and save lives.
ex.zh: 声称深度思想公司所开发的算法将会使病患受益以及挽救生命是不够的。

ex.en: Parents should be patient when children make the same mistakes repeatedly.
ex.zh: 当孩子反复犯同样的错误时，父母应该有耐心。

ex.en: The novel portrays a patriot who sacrifices personal comfort, and eventually his life, for the independence of his country.
ex.zh: 小说描绘了一位爱国者，他为了国家的独立牺牲了个人安逸，最终献出了生命。

patriotic.usage: patriot（爱国者=patr父亲+iot→把祖国当父亲对待的人）+-ic。族patriotism n.爱国主义

ex.en: Patriotic feelings can unite a nation, yet they may also be exploited to justify aggressive policies.
ex.zh: 爱国情感能够凝聚一个国家，但也可能被利用来为侵略性政策辩护。

senses: n. 巡逻；巡逻兵,警察；侦察队
patrol.usage: patr（父亲）+ol→父亲守护家人→巡查守护→巡逻。过去式patrolled，现在分词patrolling

ex.en: Guards patrol the museum at night to protect the priceless paintings from theft.
ex.zh: 保安夜间在博物馆巡逻，保护珍贵画作免遭盗窃。

ex.en: The library, funded largely by a generous patron, is open to readers free of charge.
ex.zh: 这座图书馆主要由一位慷慨的赞助人出资，免费向读者开放。

senses: n. 惠顾,光顾;资助,赞助

ex.en: The small bookshop survived thanks to the loyal patronage of neighbouring residents.
ex.zh: 这家小书店全靠邻近居民的惠顾才得以维持。

patronize.usage: v.表现出高人一等的姿态；光 顾；赞助

ex.en: Regulars have patronized the bookshop for decades, and many fear that rising rents will finally force it to close.
ex.zh: 老顾客们光顾这家书店已有数十年，许多人担心不断上涨的租金最终会迫使它关门。

senses: v. 屈尊俯就地对待;光顾,惠顾;资助,赞助

ex.en: Critics accuse the media of patronizing elderly viewers by assuming they cannot understand modern technology.
ex.zh: 批评者指责媒体以居高临下的态度对待老年观众，认为他们无法理解现代科技。

senses: n. 模范,榜样;模式,样式
n. 花样,图案;形状,方式,风格

ex.en: But the result was a new social pattern which, although it resembled European society in many ways, had a character that was distinctly American.
ex.zh: 但是,结果却是形成了一个崭新的社会格局,尽管它在很多方面与欧洲社会相似,但它具有明显的美国特色。

ex.en: Weather patterns in the region have changed noticeably over the past thirty years.
ex.zh: 过去三十年，该地区的天气模式发生了显著变化。

ex.en: Scientists have studied the migration patterns of birds across the continent.
ex.zh: 科学家研究了鸟类横贯大陆的迁徙模式。

pause.usage: 辨析:pause暂时停止;cease逐渐终止;halt行进中止步(正式);quit停止(美口语);stop一般用语

ex.en: After a brief pause, the lecturer continued to explain the most technical part of his talk.
ex.zh: 短暂停顿之后，演讲者继续讲解其报告中最专业的部分。

pave.usage: 助记:他pave(铺平)了cave(洞穴)出口的道路

ex.en: Experts warn that cutting education budgets today may pave the way for a less skilled workforce tomorrow.
ex.zh: 专家警告，今天削减教育预算可能为明天劳动力技能不足铺平道路。

ex.en: Cyclists who ride on the pavement endanger pedestrians, especially the elderly and young children.
ex.zh: 在人行道上骑行的骑车人会危及行人，尤其是老人和幼儿。

ex.en: The bear used its powerful front paw to break open the log in search of insects.
ex.zh: 熊用有力的前掌掰开木头寻找昆虫。

senses: v. 给予(注意),进行访问等
pay.usage: v.支付；偿还，缴纳；给……付 工资；付出代价；盈利 n.工资，薪水；付款；索引p413

ex.en: In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills.
ex.zh: 在这个通才辈出的时代，拥有特定的知识或技能是有利的。

ex.en: The average pay of nurses has risen more slowly than the cost of living.
ex.zh: 护士的平均工资涨幅低于生活成本的涨幅。

ex.en: It took the family three years to pay off the loan for the new car.
ex.zh: 这家人花了三年才还清新车的贷款。

senses: n. 付薪水的支票,薪金,工资

ex.en: For millions of families, an unexpected medical bill can consume an entire paycheck and push them into debt.
ex.zh: 对数百万家庭来说，一笔意料之外的医疗账单可能耗尽整月的工资，并使他们负债。

senses: n. （待付或应付的）款额，款项
payment.usage: [族] repayment n. 偿还债务；[反] non-payment n. 未支付，不支付；索引p413

ex.en: The contractor demanded an immediate payment before continuing the building work.
ex.zh: 承包商要求在继续施工前立即付款。

ex.en: Monthly payments on the loan must be made by the fifth of each month.
ex.zh: 贷款的月供必须在每月五日前支付。

ex.en: Online payment systems have made it easier for small businesses to sell to distant customers.
ex.zh: 在线支付系统使小企业更容易向远方的顾客销售。

ex.en: The insurance company agreed to a substantial payout to farmers whose crops were destroyed by last summer's drought.
ex.zh: 保险公司同意向那些农作物因去年夏天干旱而毁于一旦的农民支付一笔巨额赔款。

ex.en: The researchers crossed a wild pea with a modern variety to improve its resistance to disease.
ex.zh: 研究人员将野生豌豆与现代品种杂交，以提高其抗病性。

ex.en: After decades of conflict, the two nations finally signed a peace agreement brokered by the United Nations.
ex.zh: 经过数十年的冲突，两国最终签署了由联合国斡旋的和平协议。

senses: a. 和平的；安静的；爱好和平的
peaceful.usage: peace(和平)+ful(形容词后缀)→和平的

ex.en: The villagers led a peaceful life before the highway cut through their farmland.
ex.zh: 在高速公路穿过农田之前，村民们过着平静的生活。

ex.en: The peach orchard attracts thousands of visitors every spring when the trees burst into blossom.
ex.zh: 每年春天桃花盛开时，这片桃园吸引成千上万的游客。

books.unit: 01 前程似锦 顶峰相见

senses: a. 高峰时期的；vi. 达到最高值
peak.usage: [近] summit n. 最高点；山顶；[反] off-peak a. 非高峰期的；peak(山顶)上种不成pea(豌豆)；n.巅峰，顶点；山顶；尖顶； 帽檐 v.达到高峰 adj.高峰时期的；发音类似“匹克”→奥林匹克的精神之一就是挑战极限，到达顶峰→山峰；顶峰；易混辨析: summit指山的最高部分，喻最大数量或

ex.en: Rested in the Pacific Ocean, Mauna Kea's peak rises above the bulk of our planet's dense atmosphere.
ex.zh: 莫纳亚克山坐落于太平洋，其山峰高耸于地球大部分稠密的大气层之上。

ex.en: At its peak in 2007 it was worth some $65 billion, reckons Clare McAndrew, founder of Arts Economics, a research firm—double the figure five years earlier.
ex.zh: 据艺术经济研究公司的创始人克莱尔·麦克安德鲁估计，在2007年的巅峰时期，它(指整个艺术品市场)的总值约为650亿美元，是五年前的两倍。

ex.en: Traffic reaches its peak between seven and nine in the morning.
ex.zh: 早上七点到九点之间交通达到高峰。

ex.en: Technological innovation has propelled economic growth for decades, but its benefits have not been distributed evenly across society.
ex.zh: 几十年来，技术创新一直推动着经济增长，但其收益并未在社会中得到均匀分配。

ex.en: Warnings on food labels now highlight even tiny traces of peanut, which can trigger severe allergies.
ex.zh: 现在食品标签上的警示会标明即使微量的花生成分，因为它可能引发严重过敏。

ex.en: The garden's old pear tree still bears fruit, though its branches are heavy with age.
ex.zh: 花园里那棵老梨树仍会结果，只是枝条已被岁月压得沉甸甸。

ex.en: In the novel, the pearl symbolizes wealth that ultimately destroys rather than enriches its owner.
ex.zh: 在小说中，珍珠象征着最终毁灭而非造福主人的财富。

senses: n. 农民,农夫;未受教育的人

ex.en: The novel depicts the hard life of peasant families who migrated to cities in search of work.
ex.zh: 小说描绘了为谋生涌入城市的农民家庭的艰苦生活。

ex.en: The path was lined with smooth pebbles brought down from the mountains by ancient glaciers.
ex.zh: 小路两旁铺满光滑的鹅卵石，它们是远古冰川从山上带下来的。

ex.en: The island's peculiar climate, with dry summers and mild winters, explains why certain rare plants survive nowhere else in the country.
ex.zh: 这座岛屿奇特的气候——夏季干燥、冬季温和——解释了为什么某些珍稀植物在全国其他地方都无法存活。

senses: adj. 怪异的；特殊的；不舒服
peculiar.usage: pecu(皮裤)+li(里)+ar(人)→运动裤里穿皮裤→怪异的

ex.en: But, the force of geographic conditions peculiar to America and the sheer difficulty of maintaining old-world ways in a raw, new continent caused significant changes.
ex.zh: 但是，美国特有的地理条件的作用以及在这个原始的新大陆上维持旧世界方式的巨大困难引发了巨大的变化。

ex.en: The fruit has a peculiar smell that visitors either love or immediately dislike.
ex.zh: 这种水果有一种奇特的气味，访客要么喜欢，要么立刻反感。

ex.en: This bird species is peculiar to the islands and is found nowhere else on Earth.
ex.zh: 这种鸟是该群岛特有的，地球上其他地方都没有。

peculiarity.usage: n.特点，特性；古怪之处，怪癖

ex.en: One peculiarity of the English language is that spelling and pronunciation often fail to match.
ex.zh: 英语的一个特点在于拼写与发音常常不一致。

pedal.usage: 他在pedal(骑自行车)比赛中获得了medal(奖牌)

ex.en: She pressed the pedal harder, but the old machine refused to speed up.
ex.zh: 她把踏板踩得更用力，但这台旧机器就是提不起速。

senses: adj. 徒步的;平凡的,通俗的

ex.en: A pedestrian was slightly injured when the delivery van jumped a red light.
ex.zh: 一辆送货货车闯红灯时，一名行人受了轻伤。

ex.en: Buyers of racehorses increasingly rely on genetic testing rather than pedigree records alone to judge an animal's potential.
ex.zh: 赛马的买家越来越依赖基因检测，而不是仅仅依靠血统记录来判断一匹马的潜力。

peel.usage: 助记:peer(英国贵族)peep(偷看)入家peel(脱衣服)

ex.en: Nutritionists note that the peel of many fruits contains valuable fibre that is often thrown away.
ex.zh: 营养学家指出，许多水果的果皮含有常被丢弃的宝贵纤维。

peep.usage: 拟声词，小鸟啾啾声→偷偷看。近peek vi.偷看；glance vi.匆匆一看；助记:他坐在jeep(吉普车)里peep(偷看)；pp(两手握圈)+ee(两个小眼睛)→放双眼前作偷窥状→偷窥，偷看

ex.en: He was peeping at her through his fingers.
ex.zh: 他从指缝偷看她。

ex.en: The children took a quick peep at the presents hidden in the closet.
ex.zh: 孩子们偷看了一眼藏在衣橱里的礼物。

ex.en: The moon peeped out from behind the clouds for a moment.
ex.zh: 月亮从云层后探出头来，片刻又隐去了。

senses: n. 身份（或地位）相同的人；同龄人；同辈
n. (身份或地位)相同的人,同辈
peer.usage: [近]fellow n.同辈；contemporary n.同辈人；同龄人；pe(拍)+er(人)→同龄人打招呼喜欢拍拍肩膀→同龄人；索引p413

ex.en: That whispered message, half invitation and half forcing, is what most of us think of when we hear the words peer pressure.
ex.zh: 那种半邀请半胁迫的耳语是我们大部分人听到"同辈压力"这个词时会想到的。

ex.en: Other scientists perform the specialised work of peer review also for free, because it is a central element in the acquisition of status and the production of scientific knowledge.
ex.zh: 其他科学家进行同行专家评审的专业工作也是免费的，因为这是他们获取学术地位和产出科学知识的核心要素。

ex.en: Children learn many social skills by interacting with their peers at school.
ex.zh: 孩子们通过在学校与同龄人交往学到许多社交技能。

senses: n. [U,C] 同行评议，同行评估

ex.en: Findings that have not undergone peer-review should be reported with caution, however exciting they may appear.
ex.zh: 无论听起来多么令人兴奋，对未经同行评议的研究结果都应谨慎报道。

ex.en: Universities may expel students who repeatedly violate academic integrity rules, a punishment many administrators consider a last resort.
ex.zh: 大学可以开除屡次违反学术诚信规定的学生，许多管理者认为这是一种最后的手段。

ex.en: Before computers, journalists drafted their reports with a pen and handed them to the night editor.
ex.zh: 在电脑出现之前，记者用钢笔起草报道，然后交给夜间编辑。

ex.en: Harsher penal policies, the study finds, have failed to reduce crime rates but have greatly increased prison populations.
ex.zh: 研究发现，更严厉的刑罚政策未能降低犯罪率，却使监狱人口大幅增加。

phrases.p: increase the chance of being penalized

ex.en: The league will penalise teams whose supporters throw objects onto the pitch, even when the individuals cannot be identified.
ex.zh: 联盟将处罚其支持者向场内投掷物品的球队，即使无法查明具体的个人。

senses: v. (因犯规)处罚,惩罚;使不利,对……不公平

ex.en: Children engage in criminal behavior in that they were not sufficiently penalized for previous misdeeds.
ex.zh: 儿童从事犯罪活动，是因为他们以前的不良行为没有受到应有的惩处。

ex.en: Drivers who exceed the speed limit will be heavily penalized.
ex.zh: 超速驾驶者将受到严厉处罚。

ex.en: Critics say the new tax unfairly penalizes two-income families.
ex.zh: 批评者说，新税种对双收入家庭不公。

senses: n. [C] 点球；（运动中的）判罚
penalty.usage: pen（惩罚）+-alty→处罚。penalty kick点球；近punishment n.惩罚；拓展：penalize /'pi:nəlaɪz/ v.惩罚。；索引p413

ex.en: The current state of affairs may have been encouraged—though not justified—by the lack of legal penalty for data leakage.
ex.zh: 目前的情况可能被助长——尽管还没有得到证实——助长的原因与缺乏关于数据泄露的法律处罚有关。

ex.en: The death penalty has been abolished in many European countries.
ex.zh: 许多欧洲国家已经废除了死刑。

ex.en: Companies that violate environmental laws may face a heavy financial penalty.
ex.zh: 违反环境法的公司可能面临巨额罚款。

ex.en: Candidates must complete the answer sheet with a pencil so that the marks can be read by machine.
ex.zh: 考生必须用铅笔填写答题卡，以便机器识别标记。

ex.en: Flights were suspended for six hours after dense fog covered the airport, leaving thousands of passengers stranded.
ex.zh: 大雾笼罩机场后，航班停飞了六个小时，数千名旅客滞留。

ex.en: In economics, public opinion swings like a pendulum between confidence in markets and demands for regulation.
ex.zh: 在经济领域，公众舆论如钟摆般在信任市场与要求监管之间来回摆动。

penetrate.usage: permeate 的近义词；pe（发音类似“拍”）+net（网络）+rate（速度）→你的电脑死机了，你一直拍电脑，想“进入”网络。

ex.en: The sun's radiation penetrates the skin.
ex.zh: 太阳的辐射能透进皮肤。

ex.en: It took the police weeks to penetrate the criminal network.
ex.zh: 警方花了数周才摸清这个犯罪网络。

ex.en: Foreign brands are finding it harder to penetrate the local market.
ex.zh: 外国品牌发现要打入本地市场越来越难。

ex.en: The peninsula's economy depends heavily on fishing and on the tourists attracted by its rugged coastline.
ex.zh: 该半岛的经济严重依赖渔业以及崎岖海岸线吸引来的游客。

ex.en: The rise in prices may look small, but every penny matters to families on tight budgets.
ex.zh: 物价上涨看似微小，但对预算紧张的家庭来说每一分钱都很重要。

ex.en: Firms that dismiss staff unfairly may be required to compensate them fully, under the new employment law.
ex.zh: 根据新的就业法，不公平解雇员工的公司可能必须对员工作出全额补偿。

senses: v. 给……发养老金（退休金）
pension.usage: n.养老金；津贴，补助金 v.向（某人）支付养老金使其退 休；pen(发音类似“盼”)+sion(薪)→盼望不工作也能拿薪水的日子→退休金；索引p413

ex.en: After retiring, she lived on a modest state pension.
ex.zh: 退休后，她靠微薄的国家养老金生活。

ex.en: Many young workers worry that they will never receive a pension.
ex.zh: 许多年轻劳动者担心自己将来领不到养老金。

ex.en: The company was ordered to pay the pension it owed to retired employees.
ex.zh: 该公司被责令补发拖欠退休员工的养老金。

ex.en: Many pensioners struggle to heat their homes in winter, as energy prices rise faster than state benefits.
ex.zh: 许多领养老金的人冬天难以负担取暖费用，因为能源价格的上涨快于国家补贴。

senses: n. [pl.] 人；人们；家人；人民；群众

ex.en: Politicians often claim to speak for the people, yet polling suggests opinions differ widely across regions.
ex.zh: 政客常声称代表人民发声，但民调显示各地区观点差异很大。

ex.en: Season the meat with a little salt and freshly ground pepper.
ex.zh: 用少许盐和现磨胡椒粉给肉调味。

ex.en: He grows peppers and tomatoes in a small greenhouse behind the house.
ex.zh: 他在屋后的小温室里种植甜椒和番茄。

ex.en: The report was peppered with technical terms that few readers could understand.
ex.zh: 这份报告中满是普通读者难以理解的专业术语。

senses: 贯穿；加强意义；通过；每；自始至终

ex.en: The country now emits far less carbon per unit of output than it did two decades ago.
ex.zh: 该国现在每单位产出的碳排放远低于二十年前的水平。

ex.en: Only twenty per cent of respondents said they trusted the government's handling of the crisis, the lowest figure ever recorded.
ex.zh: 只有百分之二十的受访者表示信任政府对危机的处理，这是有记录以来的最低数字。

senses: v. 注意到；意识到；察觉到；将……理解为；将……视为；认为
v. 感知；注意到；将…理解为
perceive.usage: 词根记忆：per(through, 通过)+ceive(take, 抓住)→通过某物抓住或理解→感知；注意到；索引p413

ex.en: Look for cues about how others perceive you.
ex.zh: 寻找线索了解其他人对你怎么看。

ex.en: People who perceived greater social support were less likely to come down with a cold, and the researchers calculated that the stress-reducing effects of hugging explained about 32 percent of that beneficial effect.
ex.zh: 那些感知到更多社会支持的人更不那么容易患感冒，研究人员计算得出，拥抱的减压效果大约能解释这一有益影响32%的功效。

ex.en: How the whole image is then assembled and perceived is still a mystery although it is the subject of current research.
ex.zh: 那时整幅图像是如何被组合以及理解的尚无定论，尽管这是目前正在研究的课题。

ex.en: Nearly sixty percent of the students surveyed said they preferred online lectures to traditional seminars.
ex.zh: 受访学生中近百分之六十表示，相比传统研讨课他们更喜欢在线讲座。

senses: n. 百分比,百分率,百分数
n. 百分数，百分率，百分比
percentage.usage: n.百分比，百分率；比例；索引p413

ex.en: Only a small percentage of applicants passed the final interview.
ex.zh: 只有一小部分申请者通过了最终面试。

ex.en: The percentage of students going on to university has risen steadily.
ex.zh: 继续上大学的学生比例稳步上升。

ex.en: A high percentage of the budget is spent on public transport.
ex.zh: 预算中有很高比例用于公共交通。

ex.en: Nearly sixty per cent of the students surveyed admitted that they had never visited the library's digital archive.
ex.zh: 在接受调查的学生中，近百分之六十承认从未使用过图书馆的数字档案库。

perception.usage: n.看法，认识；感知；洞察力；索引p413

ex.en: Public perception of the drug industry has shifted sharply in recent years.
ex.zh: 近年来，公众对制药业的看法发生了急剧转变。

ex.en: Our perception of color depends largely on the light that surrounds us.
ex.zh: 我们对色彩的感知在很大程度上取决于周围的光线。

ex.en: There is a widespread perception that exams reward memory rather than understanding.
ex.zh: 人们普遍认为考试奖励的是记忆而非理解。

senses: adj. 理解力强的,有洞察力的;视觉的,听觉的,感觉的

phrases.m: 一位有洞察力的观察者

perceptive.usage: adj.有洞察力的；感觉的；索引p413

ex.en: The perceptive critic noticed details that most readers had missed.
ex.zh: 这位洞察敏锐的评论家注意到了大多数读者忽略的细节。

ex.en: She is one of the most perceptive observers of political life in the capital.
ex.zh: 她是首都政治生活最敏锐的观察者之一。

ex.en: Teachers especially value students who ask perceptive questions.
ex.zh: 教师尤其看重能提出有洞察力问题的学生。

ex.en: Infants demonstrate remarkable perceptual abilities, distinguishing human faces from other objects within hours of birth.
ex.zh: 婴儿表现出非凡的感知能力，在出生后几小时内就能把人脸与其他物体区分开来。

senses: a. 完美的；准确的；优秀的；极好的；完全的
adj. 完美的；准确的；极好的；完全的
v. 使完善，使完美，使完备
perfect.usage: adj.无瑕的，完美的 v.使完美

ex.en: The new restaurant is a perfect place for dating.
ex.zh: 那家新餐馆是约会的绝佳场所。

ex.en: After years of practice, the pianist has perfected a style all her own.
ex.zh: 经过多年练习，这位钢琴家炼就了独属于自己的风格。

ex.en: No translation can be perfect, since every language divides experience differently.
ex.zh: 没有哪种翻译能尽善尽美，因为每种语言对经验的切分都不相同。

ex.en: The craftsman spent months polishing the instrument to perfection before the concert.
ex.zh: 音乐会前，工匠花了几个月时间把这件乐器打磨得完美无缺。

ex.en: You know perfectly well what I mean.
ex.zh: 我的意思你是一清二楚的。

perform.usage: [族]performer n.表演者；[近]execute vt.执行；同义 carry out；派生 performing adj. 表演的；履行的；v.演出，表演；执行，履行；运 行，表现；起作用；索引p413

ex.en: Studies from the United States and Australia show that students who take a gap year are generally better prepared for and perform better in college than those who do not.
ex.zh: 美国和澳大利亚的研究表明，和那些直接上大学的人相比，休间隔年的学生通常做了更好的准备，在进入大学之后表现也更好。

ex.en: The orchestra will perform Beethoven's Ninth Symphony at the closing ceremony.
ex.zh: 管弦乐团将在闭幕式上演奏贝多芬第九交响曲。

ex.en: The new engine performs well at high speeds but consumes more fuel in the city.
ex.zh: 新发动机在高速下表现出色，但在市区更费油。

senses: n. 表演，演出；表现；性能；业绩；执行；履行
performance.usage: [近]show n.演出；presentation n.（戏剧等的）上演；索引p413

ex.en: Britain's new rule is a reminder to bankers that society has an interest in their performance, not just for the short term but for the long term.
ex.zh: 英国的新规定提醒银行家，社会不仅对他们的短期业绩有兴趣，而且对他们的长期业绩也有兴趣。

ex.en: Although a correlation between them leaving and subsequent bad performance at the firm is suggestive, it does not mean that such directors are always jumping off a sinking ship.
ex.zh: 尽管外部董事离任与该公司随后的糟糕表现之间的关联暗示着这一点，但这并不意味着此类董事总是在跳离"沉船"。

ex.en: Use of their gut hurt their performance on the first four tasks, as expected, and helped them on the rest.
ex.zh: 正如预期的那样，直觉的运用会影响他们在前四项任务中的表现，而对其余的任务则会有所帮助。

senses: adj. 与行动作为有关联的

phrases.m: 富有表现力的(文学)形式

ex.en: Sociologists warn that some corporate commitments to sustainability are purely performative rather than substantive.
ex.zh: 社会学家警告，一些企业对可持续发展的承诺纯属表演性质，并无实质内容。

ex.en: Audience surveys show that live performers are judged as much on their stage presence as on their technical skill.
ex.zh: 观众调查显示，人们对现场表演者的评价，看重其舞台风采的程度不亚于对其技艺的看重。

senses: vt. 使充满香气,洒香水于

ex.en: Responding to consumer pressure, the company no longer tests its perfume on animals.
ex.zh: 回应消费者的压力，该公司不再在动物身上测试香水。

ex.en: Perhaps the most striking feature of the report is its cautious tone.
ex.zh: 这份报告最引人注目的特点或许是其谨慎的语气。

ex.en: He is perhaps the finest novelist this country has ever produced.
ex.zh: 他或许是这个国家迄今产生的最优秀的小说家。

ex.en: Perhaps we should wait for more data before drawing any conclusion.
ex.zh: 也许我们应当等拿到更多数据再下结论。

senses: ③学时，课时(c) ④句点，句号
period.usage: 另 at no period 从未有过

ex.en: Unemployment fell steadily during the period following the introduction of the new training programme.
ex.zh: 在新培训计划实施后的那段时期，失业率持续下降。

periodical.usage: 辨析：magazine 大开本插图杂志；periodical 定期学术期刊；journal 有专题对象的杂志或日报

ex.en: The article, first published in a medical periodical, quickly attracted attention from policymakers.
ex.zh: 这篇最初发表在一家医学期刊上的文章很快引起了政策制定者的注意。

ex.en: The committee meets periodically to review whether the safety standards are being properly enforced.
ex.zh: 委员会定期开会，审查安全标准是否得到切实执行。

senses: ③(食物等)腐败，腐烂；(物质)老化，脆裂
perish.usage: per（彻底）+ish（去）→彻底离去→毁灭。Perish forbIdden!危险勿近！（英式警告语）；派生 perishable adj. 易腐烂的，易毁灭的

ex.en: Historians note that many ancient manuscripts perished simply because they were stored in damp conditions.
ex.zh: 历史学家指出，许多古代手稿仅仅是因存放在潮湿环境中而毁坏。

senses: adj. 永久的，持久的；永恒的
adj.（问题或困难）不断发生的
adj.（家庭住址）固定的；终身的
permanent.usage: per(一直)+man(停留)+ent(形容词后缀)→一直停留下去的→永久的；adj.永久的，永恒的；per（每一）+man（人）+ent（联想为enter“进入”）→每一个人都希望进入永恒→永久的，持久的。；① adj. 永久的；索引p413

ex.en: But the professional companies prospered in their permanent theaters, and university men with literary ambitions were quick to turn to these theaters as offering a means of livelihood.
ex.zh: 但是专业公司在他们的固定剧院里蓬勃发展，而有文学抱负的大学生迅速投身这些剧院，并将其视为谋生的手段。

ex.en: But in Osborneland, your first instinct is to fall into dependency—permanent dependency if you can get it—supported by a state only too ready to indulge your falsehood.
ex.zh: 但是在奥斯本看来，你（指失业者）的第一本能反应就是陷入对国家的依赖——如果可以获得，就一辈子依赖——我们的国家总是太愿意纵容失业者的这种错误想法了。

ex.en: The two countries signed a permanent peace agreement last year.
ex.zh: 两国去年签署了一项永久性和平协议。

ex.en: The dam altered the river's ecosystem permanently, and several fish species have already disappeared from its upper reaches.
ex.zh: 大坝永久性地改变了这条河的生态系统，几种鱼类已经从上游消失。

senses: v. 弥漫，渗透；扩散，传播
permeate.usage: per（贯穿）+me（走）+ate→走过去→渗透。近义：penetrate v. 渗透；刺入；派生permeable adj.可渗入的,可渗透的;permeation n.散布,充满；索引p413

ex.en: Democratic values and gender-equality permeate the curriculum.
ex.zh: 民主价值观和性别平等渗透在课程中。

ex.en: The smell of fresh paint permeated every room of the newly decorated office.
ex.zh: 新装修的办公室里每个房间都弥漫着新漆的气味。

ex.en: Distrust of official statistics permeates public discussion of the unemployment figures.
ex.zh: 对官方统计数据的普遍不信任，弥漫在关于失业数字的公共讨论中。

ex.en: The permeation of digital technology into everyday life has changed how people work, shop, and maintain relationships.
ex.zh: 数字技术向日常生活的渗透改变了人们工作、购物和维系人际关系的方式。

permission.usage: n.同意，许可；许可证；n.许可；批准；permit 的派生词；索引p413

ex.en: You cannot publish the photos without the photographer's permission.
ex.zh: 未经摄影师许可，你不能发表这些照片。

ex.en: Students must ask for permission before using the laboratory equipment.
ex.zh: 学生在使用实验室设备前必须获得许可。

senses: adj. 放纵的；放任的；容许的
permissive.usage: adj.放任的，纵容的；许可的；adj.放任的，纵容的；permit 的派生词；索引p413

ex.en: Critics blame permissive parenting for the rise in classroom discipline problems.
ex.zh: 批评者将课堂纪律问题增多归咎于放纵式的育儿方式。

ex.en: The country's laws on publishing are among the most permissive in the world.
ex.zh: 该国的出版法律属于世界上最宽松的。

ex.en: A permissive attitude toward small rule-breaking may invite far larger violations later.
ex.zh: 对小的违规行为持纵容态度，日后可能招致大得多的违规。

senses: n. 通行证,许可证,执照

phrases.m: 使低密度城市居住成为可能

permit.usage: [族]permission n.准许；许可；批准；[反]prohibit vt.禁止；per(通过)+mit(送)→使……能送过去→通行证；v.批准，许可 n.执照，许可证；v.批准，许可 n.许可证；per（表示“每一”，引申为“始终”）+mit（送）→每次都送，那就是“一直送”→允许；索引p413

ex.en: He was permitted to get out although he failed to finish his work.
ex.zh: 尽管他没有完成工作，但他还是获准出去了。

ex.en: Half a century of town and country planning has enabled it to retain an enviable rural coherence, while still permitting low-density urban living.
ex.zh: 半个世纪的城乡规划已经使它(指英国)在保留乡村原貌上取得了令人羡慕的成效，同时仍然实现了低密度的城市生活。

ex.en: Smoking is not permitted anywhere inside the hospital building.
ex.zh: 医院大楼内任何地方都禁止吸烟。

ex.en: Economists warn that the pernicious combination of high debt and low growth could undermine the country's recovery.
ex.zh: 经济学家警告，高债务与低增长的有害结合可能会破坏该国的复苏。

senses: a. 无休止的；一再重复的
adj. 永恒的，反复的；没完没了的
adj. 永恒的，永久的；终身的；持续的
perpetual.usage: per-（始终）+pet（寻求）+-ual→始终寻求延续的→永恒的。族perpetuate vt.使持久；同义 continuous, continual, endless, permanent, lasting；反义 temporary 暂时的；adj.长期的，永恒的；连续不断的；索引p413

ex.en: She's a perpetual student.
ex.zh: 她是个终身学习者。

ex.en: He lives in perpetual fear of losing his job.
ex.zh: 他一直生活在对失去工作的无尽恐惧之中。

ex.en: The machine was designed as a perpetual source of energy, but it violated the laws of physics.
ex.zh: 这台机器被设计成永恒的能量来源，但这违背了物理定律。

senses: v. 使永久存在,使不朽

ex.en: They perpetuate the myth of the lone genius.
ex.zh: 它们（指新的奖项）使孤独天才的神话永存。

ex.en: School textbooks sometimes perpetuate outdated stereotypes about gender and careers.
ex.zh: 学校教科书有时会使关于性别与职业的过时刻板印象延续下去。

ex.en: The system of unpaid internships perpetuates inequality between rich and poor students.
ex.zh: 无薪实习制度使贫富学生之间的不平等延续下去。

ex.en: The donor stipulated that the scholarship fund must be maintained in perpetuity, long after the university's current buildings are gone.
ex.zh: 捐赠人规定，这笔奖学金基金必须永久维持下去，即使在这所大学现有建筑消失之后也不例外。

perplex.usage: per-（彻底）+plex（折叠）→完全叠在一起理不清→使困惑。族perplexity n.困惑；perplexing a.令人费解的；同义 puzzle, confuse；反义 simplify 单一化；派生 perplexed 困惑的；perplexing 令人不解的；perplexity n. 困惑；per（每一

ex.en: They were perplexed by her response.
ex.zh: 她的答复令他们困惑不解。

ex.en: The sudden change in the company's policy perplexed many investors.
ex.zh: 公司政策的突然转变使许多投资者感到困惑。

ex.en: Her strange behaviour perplexed the doctors.
ex.zh: 她的奇怪举动使医生们感到困惑。

senses: adj. 困惑的；迷惑不解的

ex.en: We are all perplexed as to how this happened.
ex.zh: 我们都对这事是如何发生的感到困惑不已。

senses: vt. 骚扰,纠缠,为……找麻烦
persecute.usage: 派生persecution n.虐待,残害,迫害

ex.en: The regime persecuted journalists who questioned official statistics, forcing many into exile.
ex.zh: 该政权迫害质疑官方统计数据的记者，迫使许多人流亡海外。

ex.en: Her perseverance through years of rejected manuscripts finally paid off when her third novel won a major literary prize.
ex.zh: 多年来屡遭退稿，她坚持不懈，最终凭借第三部小说赢得一项重要文学奖。

senses: vi. 坚持,忍耐,百折不回,不屈不挠;支撑

phrases.m: 坚持做某事(尤指不畏困难)

persevere.usage: 派生perseverance n.坚持不懈;persevering adj.坚持的,不屈不挠的；per（贯穿始终的）+severe（严峻的，恶劣的）→在恶劣、严峻当中贯穿始终→坚持。派生：perseverance

ex.en: She persevered with her violin lessons.
ex.zh: 她孜孜不倦地学习小提琴。

ex.en: Despite repeated failures, the team persevered in its search for a cure.
ex.zh: 尽管屡遭失败，团队仍坚持寻找疗法。

ex.en: Those who persevere through hardship often gain deeper confidence in themselves.
ex.zh: 在艰难中坚持下来的人往往会获得更深的自信。

senses: vi. 持续存在；(~ in)坚持
persist.usage: 助记:per(贯穿,自始至终)+sist(站立)→持续；v.持续；坚持，执意；v.持续；坚持；per（表示“每一”）+sist（站）→每一天都站着→坚持。派生：persistent；索引p413

ex.en: The belief that the earth was flat persisted for many centuries.
ex.zh: 地球是平的这一信念持续了许多世纪。

ex.en: If the symptoms persist, you should see a doctor at once.
ex.zh: 如果症状持续存在，你应当立即就医。

ex.en: He persisted in his research despite repeated failures.
ex.zh: 尽管屡遭失败，他仍坚持自己的研究。

senses: n. 坚持,锲而不舍;持续存在,维持
persistence.usage: n.维持；坚持不懈，执意；索引p413

ex.en: Her persistence finally paid off when the company accepted her proposal.
ex.zh: 她的坚持不懈终获回报——公司接受了她的提案。

ex.en: The persistence of high unemployment is the government's biggest worry.
ex.zh: 高失业率的持续存在是政府最大的忧虑。

ex.en: Scientific progress demands patience, discipline and, above all, persistence.
ex.zh: 科学进步需要耐心、自律，更需要坚持不懈。

senses: adj. 坚持不懈的,固执的,持续的
adj. 坚持的，有毅力的；持续的
adj. 持续的；坚持不懈的
persistent.usage: persist 的派生词；词根记忆：per(throughout, 从始至终)+sist(stand, 站着)+ent(形容词后缀)→从头到尾一直站着→持续的；索引p413

ex.en: I had to be really persistent because it was very hard work.
ex.zh: 我必须坚持不懈，因为这是一项非常艰苦的工作。

ex.en: The fourth edition of the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders says "pathological gambling" involves persistent, recurring and uncontrollable pursuit less of money than of the thrill of taking risks in quest of a windfall.
ex.zh: 《心理障碍诊断与统计手册》第四版指出，"病态赌博"是指持续的、反复的、无法控制的赌博行为，与其说是为了钱，不如说是为了冒险寻求意外收获的快感。

ex.en: Persistent rain over the weekend forced the organizers to postpone the match.
ex.zh: 周末连绵不断的雨迫使主办方推迟了比赛。

ex.en: The region has persistently underperformed in education, despite repeated government initiatives and increased funding.
ex.zh: 尽管政府屡次推出举措并增加拨款，该地区的教育表现始终不佳。

senses: n. （pl. people）[C] 人；个人；（语法中的）人称

ex.en: Company policy forbids any person entering the laboratory from carrying food or drink.
ex.zh: 公司规定禁止任何人携带食物或饮料进入实验室。

senses: a. 个人的；人际的；亲自做的；私事的
personal.usage: 另 personal history 履历；另：personal fulfillment in one's work工作中的自我实现；freedom of personal expression个人言论自由；索引p413

ex.en: But it's also a lot more personal, Ortiz says, arguing that because art is so closely linked to a person, it could raise data protection and privacy problems.
ex.zh: 奥尔蒂兹说，这个问题还涉及到一些个人层面，由于艺术与个人密切相关，它可能引发数据保护和隐私问题。

ex.en: The minister keeps his personal and official life strictly separate.
ex.zh: 这位部长严格区分私事与公务。

ex.en: She made a personal appeal to the board to reconsider its decision.
ex.zh: 她以个人身份恳请董事会重新考虑其决定。

ex.en: The clinic offers personalised treatment plans based on each patient's genetic profile rather than a standard drug dosage.
ex.zh: 这家诊所根据每位患者的基因特征提供个性化治疗方案，而不是标准化的药物剂量。

senses: n. 性格，个性，人格；气质；名人

ex.en: It takes a while to judge complex aspects of personality.
ex.zh: 要判断性格的复杂方面，需要一段时间。

ex.en: Genes and upbringing both shape a child's personality in powerful ways.
ex.zh: 基因和养育都以强大的方式塑造孩子的个性。

ex.en: The talk show invites a famous personality each week to discuss current affairs.
ex.zh: 这档脱口秀每周邀请一位名人讨论时事。

senses: n. ①全体人员，全体职员

ex.en: The airline is cutting personnel costs by automating check-in at most of its domestic airports.
ex.zh: 这家航空公司通过在多数国内机场实现值机自动化来削减人事成本。

senses: ③透视画法(u)，透视图(c) ④远景，景观(c)
n. 观点；客观判断力；远景
perspective.usage: 同义 view, outlook；per（表示“每一个”）+spect（看）+ive（名词后缀）→每一面都看到，才能得出对事物的“观点”；串词记忆：思维敏捷的(perceptive)人一般都有独特的观点(perspective)；2019年阅读例：putting things into perspective 从客观的

ex.en: The exhibition provides us with a unique perspective on her work.
ex.zh: 展览为我们提供了对她的作品的独特视角。

ex.en: This long perspective makes the pessimistic view of our prospects seem more likely to be a passing fad.
ex.zh: 这种长远的视角使我们未来的悲观看法看上去更像是一时的流行。

ex.en: Travelling abroad can give young people a broader perspective on the world.
ex.zh: 出国旅行能让年轻人以更开阔的视野看待世界。

ex.en: Success, the coach reminded the team, comes from perspiration far more than from inspiration.
ex.zh: 教练提醒队员们，成功更多来自汗水，而非灵感。

perspire.usage: per（每一个）+spir（呼吸）→皮肤每个地方都在呼吸，方式就是流汗

ex.en: He mopped his perspiring face with a handkerchief.
ex.zh: 他用手帕擦去脸上的汗水。

senses: v. 劝说；说服；使信服；使相信

ex.en: Nothing could persuade me to return to the kind of life Kelsey used to advocate and I once enjoyed.
ex.zh: 没有什么能说服我回到凯尔西曾经提倡的、我也曾经享受过的那种生活。

ex.en: If that happens, passionate consumers would try to persuade others to boycott products, putting the reputation of the target company at risk.
ex.zh: 如果上述情形发生的话，情绪激动的消费者会设法劝说其他人抵制产品，从而危及目标公司的声誉。

ex.en: The charity used moving stories to persuade the public to donate.
ex.zh: 该慈善机构用感人的故事说服公众捐款。

persuasion.usage: persuade（说服）的名词。persuasion指说服的行为；persuasiveness指有说服力；n.说服，劝服；信仰；索引p413

ex.en: Relying on ethical persuasion rather than law to address the misuse of body ideals may be the best step.
ex.zh: 依赖道德说服而非法律来解决体型理想的误用可能是最好的举措。

ex.en: Gentle persuasion proved more effective than threats in persuading residents to recycle.
ex.zh: 事实证明，温和的劝说比威胁更能促使居民进行回收。

ex.en: Politicians of every persuasion attended the ceremony, from conservatives to socialists.
ex.zh: 持各种政治信仰的人士都出席了典礼，从保守派到社会主义者。

senses: adj. 劝说的,劝诱的;有说服力的
persuasive.usage: adj.有说服力的，能使人信服的；索引p413

ex.en: Her persuasive presentation convinced the council to fund the new library.
ex.zh: 她极具说服力的陈述使议会同意为新图书馆拨款。

ex.en: The evidence for climate change is persuasive even to former skeptics.
ex.zh: 气候变化的证据连从前的怀疑者也为之信服。

ex.en: Much advertising relies on persuasive images rather than facts.
ex.zh: 许多广告依靠的是有说服力的画面而非事实。

ex.en: With times changing, the old rules don't pertain any more.
ex.zh: 随着时代的变化，旧的规则不再适用了。

senses: adj. 弥漫的;渗透的;普遍的

ex.en: Advertising has become so pervasive in public spaces that several cities have restricted billboards near schools.
ex.zh: 广告在公共场所已变得无孔不入，以至于一些城市限制了学校附近的广告牌。

ex.en: Critics dismiss such pessimism about artificial intelligence as speculation, pointing to decades of exaggerated predictions.
ex.zh: 批评人士认为，这种对人工智能的悲观论调纯属臆测，并指出几十年来类似预言总是言过其实。

ex.en: Despite recent setbacks, the report rejects deep pessimism about the country's long-term economic prospects.
ex.zh: 尽管近期遭遇挫折，该报告仍拒绝对该国长期经济前景抱深度悲观态度。

senses: n. 悲观论者，悲观主义者

ex.en: A committed pessimist expects the worst, yet planners argue that preparing for failure is simply prudent management.
ex.zh: 坚定的悲观主义者预期最坏的结果，但规划者认为，为失败做好准备只是审慎的管理方式。

pessimistic.usage: 派生 pessimism n. 悲观，悲观主义；pessimist n. 悲观主义者，悲观论者；adj.悲观的，悲观主义的；pessi（联想成怕是）+mistic（联想成 mistake 错误）→总怕犯错受批评，对待生活有点悲观；索引p413

ex.en: This long perspective makes the pessimistic view of our prospects seem more likely to be a passing fad.
ex.zh: 这种长远视角使对人类前景的悲观观点看起来更像一个短暂的风潮。

ex.en: Some commentators are pessimistic about the future of printed newspapers.
ex.zh: 一些评论者对印刷报纸的前景感到悲观。

senses: n. 害虫;讨厌的人(或物)

ex.en: Scientists bred a rice variety that resists the pest without heavy pesticide use.
ex.zh: 科学家培育出一种水稻品种，无需大量农药即可抵御这种害虫。

pesticide.usage: n.杀虫剂，农药；pest（害虫）+cide（砍，杀）→杀死害虫→杀虫剂

ex.en: The production and application of fertilisers and pesticides account for the largest part of energy use in the modern industrialized agricultural process.
ex.zh: 在现代工业化的农业进程中，化肥和杀虫剂的生产和使用占能源使用的最大部分。

ex.en: A growing number of hotels now welcome guests travelling with a pet.
ex.zh: 越来越多的酒店现在欢迎携带宠物的客人入住。

ex.en: Each petal of the orchid is patterned to guide insects toward the centre of the flower.
ex.zh: 兰花的每一片花瓣都有引导昆虫飞向花心的图案。

senses: n. (向法院递交的)申请书;正式的请求
petition.usage: pet（寻求）+-ition→寻求当局回应的文书→请愿书。petitioner n.请愿人；n.请愿书；申诉书 v.请愿，请求；起诉；索引p413

ex.en: In response to another petition last year about banning fake lawns, which gathered 30,000 signatures, the government responded that it has "no plans to ban the use of artificial grass".
ex.zh: 去年，另一份关于禁止人造草坪的请愿书收集了3万个签名，对这份请愿书，政府回应说，它“没有禁止使用人造草坪的计划”。

ex.en: Residents signed a petition against the construction of the new highway.
ex.zh: 居民们在反对修建新高速公路的请愿书上签了字。

ex.en: The workers petitioned the government to raise the minimum wage.
ex.zh: 工人们向政府请愿，要求提高最低工资。

ex.en: The museum's fossil collection shows how ancient forests were gradually petrified into stone over millions of years.
ex.zh: 博物馆的化石收藏展示了古代森林如何在数百万年间逐渐石化。

ex.en: The government plans to raise petrol taxes to fund public transport and discourage car use.
ex.zh: 政府计划提高汽油税，为公共交通筹资并抑制汽车使用。

ex.en: The country's economy still depends heavily on petroleum exports, despite official promises to diversify.
ex.zh: 尽管官方承诺实现多元化，该国经济仍然严重依赖石油出口。

senses: adj. 小的,琐碎的;气量小的
petty.usage: pet（小块）+-ty→小块的→琐碎的。petty officer海军士官；petty cash零用现金

ex.en: Managers are advised to ignore petty disputes among staff and focus on genuine performance issues.
ex.zh: 管理者被建议不要理会员工间琐碎的争执，而应关注真实的绩效问题。

ex.en: Patients with aphasia struggle to speak although their intelligence is unaffected, a condition that often follows a stroke.
ex.zh: 失语症患者说话困难，但智力并不受影响，这种病症常在中风后出现。

ex.en: The tomb of the pharaoh remained undisturbed for over three thousand years before its discovery.
ex.zh: 这位法老的陵墓在被发现前的三千多年里从未被打扰。

ex.en: Pharmaceutical companies argue that high prices are needed to fund risky research into new drugs.
ex.zh: 制药公司辩称，高昂的药价是为新药的高风险研究提供资金所必需的。

senses: n. 药剂学,配药业,制药业;药房
pharmacy.usage: 助记:pharma(药)+cy(名词后缀)→药剂学

ex.en: Customers can now collect prescribed medicine directly from the pharmacy attached to the clinic.
ex.zh: 患者现在可以直接在诊所附设的药房领取处方药。

ex.en: The new curriculum places greater emphasis on practical skills than on the memorisation of facts.
ex.zh: 新课程更加注重实用技能，而非对事实的死记硬背。

senses: n. (天文、物理学等的)相,相位

ex.en: The project will enter its final phase once the funding for field trials is approved.
ex.zh: 一旦实地试验的资金获批，该项目将进入最后阶段。

ex.en: Only a small fraction of PhD graduates find permanent academic positions, according to a nationwide survey of doctoral employment.
ex.zh: 根据一项关于博士就业的全国调查，只有一小部分博士毕业生能获得长期的学术职位。

ex.en: The aurora is a natural phenomenon caused by charged particles from the sun colliding with gases in the upper atmosphere.
ex.zh: 极光是一种自然现象，由来自太阳的带电粒子与高层大气中的气体碰撞而形成。

senses: n. (pl. phenomena)(自然、社会、历史的)现象
n. 现象；非凡的人（或事物）
phenomenon.usage: n.现象；杰出非凡的人；n.现象；杰出的人，非凡 的人；索引p414

ex.en: Globalization is a phenomenon of the 21st century.
ex.zh: 全球化是21世纪的现象。

ex.en: The Northern Lights are a natural phenomenon that attracts many tourists.
ex.zh: 北极光是一种吸引众多游客的自然现象。

ex.en: Urbanization is a global phenomenon that is changing the way people live.
ex.zh: 城市化是一种正在改变人们生活方式的全球现象。

senses: adj. (用于乐队、音乐团体等名称中)爱好音乐的
philharmonic.usage: 真 the New York Philharmonic 纽约爱乐乐团；索引p414

ex.en: The city's philharmonic orchestra offers discounted tickets to students to attract younger audiences.
ex.zh: 该市爱乐乐团向学生提供折扣票，以吸引更年轻的观众。

senses: n. 哲学家；善于思考的人

ex.en: The Greek philosopher argued that knowledge begins with doubt.
ex.zh: 这位希腊哲学家主张知识始于怀疑。

ex.en: Enlightenment philosophers believed that reason could improve the human condition.
ex.zh: 启蒙哲学家们相信理性能够改善人类的境况。

ex.en: He is regarded as the philosopher who brought Western ideas to a wider Chinese audience.
ex.zh: 他被视为把西方思想带给更广泛中国读者的哲人。

senses: adj. 哲学的;达观的,处乱不惊的
adj. 哲学的；处乱不惊的

ex.en: The first chapter examines the philosophical foundations of modern science.
ex.zh: 第一章考察了现代科学的哲学基础。

ex.en: Facing the loss calmly, she took a philosophical view of life.
ex.zh: 她平静地面对损失，对生活抱着达观的态度。

ex.en: His interest in philosophical questions dates back to his college years.
ex.zh: 他对哲学问题的兴趣可以追溯到大学时代。

senses: n. 生活的信条(或态度)
philosophy.usage: n.哲学；哲学体系，思想体系；索引p414

ex.en: It was with these great revelations that a new kind of philosophy founded in reason was born.
ex.zh: 正是由于这些重大的(真相)揭示，一种建立在理性基础上的新型哲学才得以诞生。

ex.en: The company's philosophy is that happy employees serve customers better.
ex.zh: 该公司的理念是：员工快乐才能更好地服务顾客。

ex.en: She studied philosophy at university, focusing on ethics and political thought.
ex.zh: 她在大学学习哲学，重点是伦理学和政治思想。

ex.en: Surveys show that most teenagers check their phone within minutes of waking up.
ex.zh: 调查显示，大多数青少年在醒来后几分钟内就会查看手机。

ex.en: The scheme promised guaranteed returns, but investigators quickly exposed it as a phoney investment designed to cheat elderly savers.
ex.zh: 该计划承诺保证回报，但调查人员很快揭穿它是一个旨在欺骗老年储户的虚假投资。

ex.en: She pinned the old photo above her desk, a reminder of the village school where she had taught thirty years earlier.
ex.zh: 她把那张旧照片钉在书桌上方，提醒自己想起三十年前任教的那所乡村学校。

ex.en: The exhibition pairs each photograph with a short text explaining where and why the image was taken.
ex.zh: 展览为每张照片配上一段简短的文字，说明照片拍摄的地点和缘由。

ex.en: The war photographer risked his life repeatedly, believing that images could change public opinion faster than official reports.
ex.zh: 这位战地摄影记者多次冒着生命危险，因为他相信影像比官方报告更能迅速改变公众舆论。

senses: a. 摄影的；摄制的；照片的

ex.en: The witness claimed to have a photographic memory, yet her description of the suspect changed several times under questioning.
ex.zh: 这名目击者声称自己有过目不忘的记忆力，但在盘问中她对嫌疑人的描述却数次变化。

ex.en: Modern smartphones allow amateurs to take photographs of a quality that once demanded expensive professional equipment.
ex.zh: 现代智能手机让业余爱好者也能拍出昔日需要昂贵专业设备才能达到的照片质量。

senses: n. 短语，词组，惯用语；成语
phrase.usage: 学习短语phrase要分阶段phase进行

ex.en: He just comes out with the same old stock phrases.
ex.zh: 他总说那些同样的陈词滥调。

ex.en: The phrase “carbon footprint” entered everyday speech within a decade of its coinage.
ex.zh: “碳足迹”一词被造出来后不出十年便进入了日常语言。

ex.en: She phrased the refusal so politely that no one took offence.
ex.zh: 她措辞极为礼貌地表示拒绝，以致无人感到被冒犯。

senses: n. 措辞,用语;乐句划分法,分句法

ex.en: Diplomats spent weeks negotiating the precise phrasing of the statement, since a single word could alter its legal meaning.
ex.zh: 外交官们花了数周时间磋商声明的确切措辞，因为一个词就可能改变其法律含义。

ex.en: The lecture traces how physics emerged from natural philosophy during the scientific revolution of the seventeenth century.
ex.zh: 讲座追溯了物理学如何在十七世纪科学革命期间从自然哲学中脱胎而出。

senses: adj. 自然科学的,物理的
adj. 物质的；物理学的；身体的，肉体的，躯体的；有形的
adj. 实物的；外在的；物理的；身体的
physical.usage: adj.身体的；物质的；外 形的；物理的 n.体检；索引p414

ex.en: Rather than portraying landscape, land artists used the physical substance of the land itself as their medium.
ex.zh: 地景艺术家使用土地本身的物质作为媒介，而不是描绘风光。

ex.en: Regular physical exercise can reduce the risk of heart disease.
ex.zh: 经常进行体育锻炼可以降低患心脏病的风险。

ex.en: There is no physical evidence to support his claim.
ex.zh: 没有实物证据支持他的说法。

senses: adv. 身体上,肉体上;依据自然规律;实际上,根本上

ex.en: Regular exercise keeps children not only physically healthy but also more focused in class.
ex.zh: 经常锻炼不仅使儿童身体健康，也让他们上课时更加专注。

physician.usage: [近]doctor n.医生；大夫；physic(身体)+ian(人)→和你身体打交道的人→医生

ex.en: He became the President's personal physician.
ex.zh: 他成了总统的私人医生。

ex.en: The physician advised the patient to reduce salt intake and exercise regularly.
ex.zh: 内科医生建议病人减少盐的摄入并经常锻炼。

ex.en: Many rural counties face a shortage of trained physicians willing to work in remote areas.
ex.zh: 许多农村县面临愿意到偏远地区工作的训练有素的医生短缺问题。

ex.en: The physicist was awarded the prize for research that bridged quantum theory and cosmology.
ex.zh: 这位物理学家因连接量子理论与宇宙学的研究而获奖。

senses: n. 物理（指学科或课程）
physics.usage: [族] physical a.物理学的；physicist n.物理学家；n.物理学；索引p414

ex.en: She won a scholarship to study physics at one of the country's leading universities.
ex.zh: 她获得奖学金，到该国一所顶尖大学学习物理。

ex.en: Engineers apply the laws of physics to design safer bridges and faster trains.
ex.zh: 工程师运用物理定律来设计更安全的桥梁和更快的列车。

ex.en: Modern physics began when Einstein questioned the assumptions of classical mechanics.
ex.zh: 当爱因斯坦质疑经典力学的假设时，现代物理学开始了。

ex.en: The physiologist measured how athletes' bodies respond to training at high altitude.
ex.zh: 这位生理学家测量了运动员的身体在高海拔训练时的反应。

ex.en: First-year medical students study the basics of human physiology.
ex.zh: 医学院一年级学生学习人体生理学基础。

ex.en: Regular exercise produces measurable changes in the body's physiology.
ex.zh: 经常锻炼会使身体机能产生可测量的变化。

ex.en: Advances in plant physiology have helped farmers raise crop yields.
ex.zh: 植物生理学的进步帮助农民提高了作物产量。

ex.en: The athlete's powerful physique is the product of disciplined training rather than exceptional natural talent, his coach insists.
ex.zh: 他的教练坚持认为，这名运动员强健的体格是严格训练的产物，而非异于常人的天赋。

ex.en: Learning the piano demands patience, but studies link it to improved memory in children.
ex.zh: 学钢琴需要耐心，但研究表明它与儿童记忆力的提升有关。

senses: n. [sing.] 挑选；[C] 选中的人（或物）

ex.en: Consumers increasingly pick products based on environmental labels rather than brand names.
ex.zh: 消费者越来越多地根据环保标签而非品牌名称来挑选产品。

ex.en: Sales of electric pickup trucks rose sharply after the new subsidies were announced.
ex.zh: 新补贴政策公布后，电动皮卡的销量大幅上升。

ex.en: Families gathered in the park for a picnic as soon as the warm weather arrived.
ex.zh: 温暖的天气一来，各家各户便聚到公园里野餐。

ex.en: The novel depicts rural life with such precision that readers can almost smell the hay and hear the church bells.
ex.zh: 这部小说以极为精细的笔触描绘乡村生活，读者几乎能闻到干草的气息，听到教堂的钟声。

ex.en: The report paints a grim picture of housing conditions for low-income families.
ex.zh: 该报告描绘了低收入家庭住房状况的严峻图景。

ex.en: The bakery sells out of its apple pie before noon on weekends.
ex.zh: 周末这家面包店的苹果派不到中午就销售一空。

senses: n. (一)件,(一)片,(一)篇;碎片,断片

ex.en: The evidence, taken piece by piece, eventually persuaded the jury of the defendant's innocence.
ex.zh: 这些证据被逐一梳理后，最终让陪审团相信了被告的清白。

senses: adj. 零散的;逐渐的;零敲碎打的

ex.en: Critics complain that the government's piecemeal reforms have created a confusing patchwork of rules rather than a coherent policy.
ex.zh: 批评者抱怨说，政府零敲碎打的改革造就了规则琐碎混杂的局面，而非连贯的政策。

senses: vt. (以目光、洞察力等)看透,识破
pierce.usage: 近penetrate v.穿透；刺入。pierce one's heart刺痛某人的心（比喻）；一块玻璃碎片(piece)刺破(pierce)了他的手掌

ex.en: The arrow pierced his shoulder.
ex.zh: 箭射入他的肩膀。

ex.en: A siren pierced the silence of the night.
ex.zh: 警笛声划破了夜的寂静。

ex.en: Her sharp questions pierced the weak points of his argument.
ex.zh: 她犀利的提问看穿了他论证中的薄弱之处。

ex.en: Scientists study the pig because its organs closely resemble those of humans.
ex.zh: 科学家研究猪，因为猪的器官与人类的十分相似。

ex.en: Researchers trained a pigeon to distinguish between paintings by different artists.
ex.zh: 研究人员训练一只鸽子分辨不同画家的作品。

ex.en: Inspectors described the conditions in the abandoned farmhouse as a pigsty, with rubbish piled against every wall.
ex.zh: 检查人员形容那座废弃农舍的状况像个猪圈，垃圾堆满了每一面墙的墙根。

ex.en: Residents piled sandbags along the river bank throughout the night as flood warnings were issued for the third time.
ex.zh: 洪水预警第三次发布，居民们彻夜在河岸堆放沙袋。

pile.usage: 考点:pile up堆积,积聚;pile on夸张;pile into挤入;pile with用……堆积

ex.en: A pile of unread reports on her desk reflected the department's chronic staff shortage.
ex.zh: 她桌上堆积如山的未读报告反映出该部门长期人手不足。

senses: n. [C] 朝圣者；（美国的）移民先驱
v. 朝山进香,朝圣;流浪
pilgrim.usage: pil（堆）+grim→经历长途跋涉的人→朝圣者。Pilgrim Fathers五月花号清教徒；派生pilgrimage n.朝圣之行；索引p414

ex.en: Every year thousands of pilgrims travel to the ancient temple to pray.
ex.zh: 每年都有成千上万的朝圣者前往那座古庙祈祷。

ex.en: The early pilgrims crossed the ocean in search of religious freedom.
ex.zh: 早期的移民先驱为寻求宗教自由横渡大洋。

ex.en: For centuries the inn has sheltered pilgrims on their long journey.
ex.zh: 几百年来，这家客栈一直为长途跋涉的朝圣者提供落脚之处。

senses: n. 药丸,药片;讨厌的人
pill.usage: 谚:Bitter pills may have wholesome effects.良药苦口利于病

ex.en: Doctors warn that no pill can replace a balanced diet and regular exercise.
ex.zh: 医生警告，没有任何药丸能替代均衡的饮食和经常锻炼。

ex.en: Trust between citizens and institutions is a pillar of a functioning democracy.
ex.zh: 公民与机构之间的信任是民主制度有效运转的支柱。

ex.en: Hotels discovered that guests judge comfort largely by the quality of the pillow.
ex.zh: 酒店发现，客人对舒适度的评判很大程度上取决于枕头的好坏。

senses: vt. 驾驶（飞行器）；领航（船只）
n. 飞行员,驾驶员,领航员,舵手
pilot.usage: [近]experimental a.试验的；词组pilot through for使某事(如新法律)得以通过

ex.en: The airline trained every pilot on new simulators before the aircraft entered service.
ex.zh: 在新机型投入运营前，航空公司让每名飞行员在新模拟器上受训。

pin.usage: 词组on pins and needles如坐针毡

ex.en: The tailor secured the paper pattern with a pin before cutting the fabric.
ex.zh: 裁缝在裁剪布料前用别针把纸样固定住。

senses: v. 使不舒服,使为难;捏,拧,夹
pinch.usage: 助记:我们要pinch(节约)每一inch(英寸)土地

ex.en: Add a pinch of salt to balance the sweetness of the sauce.
ex.zh: 加一撮盐来平衡酱汁的甜味。

ex.en: The pine survives harsh winters by keeping its needles, which shed snow easily.
ex.zh: 松树凭借不易积雪的针叶在严冬中存活。

ex.en: The flamingo's famous pink colour comes from pigments in the tiny creatures it eats.
ex.zh: 火烈鸟著名的粉红色来自它所摄食的微小生物中的色素。

senses: v. 明确指出,确定(位置或时间);准确解释(或说明)

ex.en: Engineers eventually pinpointed the fault to a single cracked sensor, a component costing less than ten pounds.
ex.zh: 工程师最终把故障精确定位到一个开裂的传感器上，这个部件的价格还不到十英镑。

senses: n. 品脱(液量单位,为1/8加仑)

ex.en: The recipe calls for half a pint of milk stirred slowly into the batter.
ex.zh: 这份食谱需要半品脱牛奶，慢慢搅入面糊中。

senses: n. 先驱,倡导者,开拓者
v. 倡导；开创；当开拓者,当先锋
pioneer.usage: [近]forerunner n.先驱者；派生pioneering adj.开拓性的；探索性的；pi(披)+one(一个人)+er(人)→披荆斩棘的一个人→先锋，先驱

ex.en: Two anthropologist-linguists were pioneers in describing many native languages of North and South America during the first half of the twentieth century.
ex.zh: 这两位人类语言学家是20世纪上半叶描述北美和南美许多土著语言的先驱。

ex.en: The laboratory pioneered the use of computers in medical diagnosis.
ex.zh: 这家实验室开创了计算机在医学诊断中的应用。

ex.en: She was a pioneer of women's education in her country.
ex.zh: 她是本国女性教育的开拓者。

phrases.m: 白日梦；想入非非的计划

ex.en: Engineers replaced the corroded pipe before leaks could contaminate the town's water supply.
ex.zh: 工程师在泄漏污染镇上的供水之前更换了锈蚀的管道。

ex.en: The company has several new drugs in the pipeline, although none is expected to reach the market before 2030.
ex.zh: 该公司有多种新药正在研发之中，但预计在2030年之前不会有任何一种上市。

senses: n. 海盗；盗印者,盗版者,侵犯专利权者
vt. 盗印,盗版,掠夺,翻印
pirate.usage: 派生piratic(al) adj.海盗(似)的；剽窃的,侵犯版权的,翻印的

ex.en: The software pirate was fined heavily for selling counterfeit programs online.
ex.zh: 这名盗版者因在网上销售假冒软件被处以重罚。

phrases.p: hold a pistol to one's head
phrases.m: 以恐吓方式使某人从命

ex.en: The museum displays a duelling pistol from the eighteenth century, complete with its original case.
ex.zh: 博物馆展出了一把十八世纪的决斗用手枪，连原来的枪盒都在。

pit.usage: [近]hole n.洞；mine n.矿；矿井；助记:pig(猪)掉进了pit(坑)里

ex.en: Archaeologists found animal bones in a pit that dates back roughly four thousand years.
ex.zh: 考古学家在一个约四千年前的坑穴中发现了动物骨骼。

senses: n. [C,U]程度；力度；（事物的）最高点
pitch.usage: sales pitch 推销游说的话术；助记:矿工在pit(矿井)旁pitch(搭帐篷)

ex.en: Workers heated the pitch before sealing the roof against the winter rain.
ex.zh: 工人们先加热沥青，然后密封屋顶以抵御冬雨。

pity.usage: [近]sympathy n.同情；[反]merciless a.无慈悲心的

ex.en: It is a pity that so many valuable manuscripts remain locked in private collections.
ex.zh: 令人遗憾的是，这么多珍贵手稿仍被锁在私人收藏中。

senses: n. 枢轴;枢纽;中心点;关键人物

ex.en: Facing declining sales, the firm decided to pivot from hardware manufacturing to software services.
ex.zh: 面对销售额下滑，该公司决定从硬件制造转向软件服务。

ex.en: Nutritionists warn that eating pizza several times a week can significantly increase daily intake of salt and saturated fat.
ex.zh: 营养学家警告，每周吃几次比萨会大大增加每日的盐和饱和脂肪摄入量。

ex.en: In the dictionary, the abbreviation pl. marks a noun that usually appears in the plural form.
ex.zh: 在词典中，缩写 pl. 标示通常以复数形式出现的名词。

place.usage: [族]placebo n.安慰剂；[近]put v.放；小记：in place 在正确位置，准备就绪；in place of 代替，顶替；in the first place 起初；take place 发生，进行；place emphasis on 重视；索引p414

ex.en: Quotas get action: they "open the way to equality and they break through the glass ceiling," according to Reding, a result seen in France and other countries with legally binding provisions on placing women in top business positions.
ex.zh: 定额能带来切实的行动：它们可以"开启平等之路，打破（阻碍女性晋升的）玻璃天花板"，Reding如是说，这一结果见于法国和其他对女性进入企业高管职位有法律约束力条款的国家。

ex.en: She placed the documents carefully in the bottom drawer.
ex.zh: 她把文件小心地放进最底层的抽屉。

ex.en: The city has become one of the most expensive places in the world to live in.
ex.zh: 这座城市已成为世界上生活成本最高的地方之一。

senses: n. （对物件的）安置；（对人的）安排

ex.en: If we were really bold, we might even begin to think of high-calorie fast food in the same way as cigarettes—by setting strict limits on advertising, product placement and sponsorship of sports events," he said.
ex.zh: 他说："如果我们真的够勇敢，我们甚至可以开始用看待香烟的方式来看待高热量的快餐——对其广告、植入式营销以及体育赛事赞助实施严格的限制。"

senses: n. 抄袭,剽窃,剽窃作品(c/u)
plagiarism.usage: 派生plagiarist n.剽窃者,抄袭者

ex.en: Universities now run every thesis through software designed to detect plagiarism.
ex.zh: 大学现在用专门软件检测每篇论文是否存在抄袭。

phrases.m: 城市化带来的其他灾难

plague.usage: [近]afflict vt.折磨；困扰；本身为词根，意为“瘟疫”；[近] epidemic n. 流行病；[近] trouble vt. 使烦恼；索引p414

ex.en: The plague swept through the crowded city, killing thousands within months.
ex.zh: 瘟疫席卷这座拥挤的城市，数月之内夺去数千人的生命。

ex.en: The team has been plagued by injuries throughout the season.
ex.zh: 整个赛季，球队一直饱受伤病困扰。

ex.en: For users of older systems, computer viruses remain a plague.
ex.zh: 对老系统的用户来说，计算机病毒仍是一大祸患。

senses: a. 简单的；朴素的； plain text 纯文本
adj. 简单的；朴素的；平坦的
adj. 明白的,易懂的;朴素的
adj. 坦率的;平凡的,普通的
plain.usage: [近]simple a.简单的；plateau n.高原；adj.朴素的；单纯的；显而易 见的；清楚的；坦率的；普通 的 adv.完全地，简直 n.平原

ex.en: The vast plain stretches for hundreds of miles toward the horizon.
ex.zh: 广袤的平原绵延数百英里，直抵天际。

ex.en: The safety instructions are written in plain language.
ex.zh: 安全说明用的是平实的语言。

ex.en: She wore a plain grey dress to the interview.
ex.zh: 她穿了一条式样朴素的灰色连衣裙去面试。

ex.en: The plaintiff claimed that the company had ignored repeated complaints about the faulty brakes.
ex.zh: 原告声称，该公司对有关刹车故障的多次投诉置之不理。

ex.en: The plaintiff argued that the company had ignored safety warnings issued years earlier.
ex.zh: 原告辩称，该公司无视多年前发出的安全警告。

senses: n. 计划,规划;平面图,设计图

ex.en: The government plans to invest heavily in renewable energy over the next decade.
ex.zh: 政府计划在未来十年大力投资可再生能源。

ex.en: The council approved a five-year plan to improve public transport.
ex.zh: 市议会批准了一项改善公共交通的五年计划。

ex.en: Their plan to open a second store was delayed by rising costs.
ex.zh: 他们开设第二家店铺的计划因成本上升而推迟。

ex.en: Engineers redesigned the wing after tests showed the plane consumed more fuel than predicted.
ex.zh: 测试显示这架飞机的油耗高于预期后，工程师重新设计了机翼。

ex.en: Astronomers have identified a planet whose atmosphere may contain water vapour.
ex.zh: 天文学家已确认一颗大气层中可能含有水蒸气的行星。

ex.en: The new plant will create hundreds of jobs, though critics question its environmental impact.
ex.zh: 这座新工厂将创造数百个就业岗位，但批评者质疑其环境影响。

ex.en: Working conditions on the tea plantation improved after international buyers demanded stricter standards.
ex.zh: 在国际买家要求更严格的标准后，茶叶种植园的工作条件得到改善。

ex.en: Single-use plastics have been banned in several countries after images of polluted beaches spread widely online.
ex.zh: 在受污染海滩的照片在网上广泛传播后，一些国家已经禁用一次性塑料制品。

senses: v. 抹灰,粉饰;粘贴,涂抹

ex.en: Cracked plaster covered the walls of the abandoned house.
ex.zh: 这座弃屋的墙上布满开裂的灰泥。

ex.en: She put a plaster on the cut to keep it clean.
ex.zh: 她在伤口上贴了一片创可贴以保持清洁。

ex.en: The workers plastered the inner walls before the painting began.
ex.zh: 粉刷开始前，工人们先给内墙抹了灰。

senses: a. 塑料的；（指材料）可塑的

ex.en: The pipes should be made of plastic.
ex.zh: 这些管子应该是用塑料制作的。

ex.en: Many supermarkets have stopped giving customers free plastic bags.
ex.zh: 许多超市已不再向顾客提供免费塑料袋。

ex.en: The toy is molded from soft plastic, so it is safe for babies.
ex.zh: 这个玩具由软塑料模压而成，对婴儿来说是安全的。

ex.en: The collector paid a high price for a rare eighteenth-century porcelain plate.
ex.zh: 收藏家为一只罕见的十八世纪瓷盘出了高价。

senses: n. (发展或增长后的)稳定期,停滞期
v. 保持稳定水平,处于停滞状态
plateau.usage: 联想记忆: plat(flat, 平坦的)+eau→稳定的→稳定期；索引p414

ex.en: Workers tended to be diligent for the first few days of the week in any case, before hitting a plateau and then slackening off.
ex.zh: 在任何情况下，工人在一周的前几天往往都比较卖力，继而达到一个稳定水平，然后开始松懈。

ex.en: After climbing for six hours they finally reached a broad plateau.
ex.zh: 攀行六小时后，他们终于登上了一片宽阔的高原。

ex.en: Sales rose sharply for two years and then hit a plateau.
ex.zh: 销售额连续两年猛增，随后进入停滞期。

phrases.p: be at home on the platform

platform.usage: [近] stage n. 舞台；词根记忆: plat(flat, 平的)+form(shape, 形状)→形状平的地方→平台；索引p414

ex.en: The train to Manchester will leave from platform six.
ex.zh: 开往曼彻斯特的列车将从 6 号站台发车。

ex.en: Social media platforms face growing pressure to remove false information.
ex.zh: 社交媒体平台在删除虚假信息方面面临越来越大的压力。

ex.en: Education reform stands at the center of the party's platform.
ex.zh: 教育改革处于该党政纲的核心位置。

senses: adj. (论点等)貌似有理的,(说法等)似乎有道理的
adj. (指人)能说会道的(尤指行骗),花言巧语的
adj. 有道理的，可信的；花言巧语的
plausible.usage: [近] reasonable a. 合理的；plaus（拍手）+-ible→众人拍手赞成，都说他的话讲得通→有道理的；plaus（拍手，鼓掌）+ible（后缀）→值得鼓掌的事应是“可信的”。；词根记忆: plaus(strike, 敲)+ible(形容词后缀)→敲锣叫好的→貌似合理的；索引p414

ex.en: The supposed importance of influentials derives from a plausible-sounding but largely untested theory called the "two step flow of communication".
ex.zh: 这种有影响力人士的所谓重要性源于一个听起来似乎合情合理但多半未经证实的“两级传播理论”。

ex.en: The detective admitted that the suspect's story sounded plausible, but the evidence told another story.
ex.zh: 侦探承认嫌疑人的说法听起来可信，但证据讲述的却是另一回事。

ex.en: The paper offers a plausible explanation for the sudden decline in bee populations.
ex.zh: 这篇论文为蜂群数量的骤降提供了一个看似合理的解释。

ex.en: She could plausibly claim that the delay was caused by circumstances beyond her control, so the committee accepted her explanation.
ex.zh: 她可以令人信服地声称延误是由她无法控制的情况造成的，因此委员会接受了她的解释。
